summary: The authors identify Avp and Oxt as downregulated after day-10 pituitary stalk lesion. Both registered effects are negative, and neither reaches registered FDR < 0.05. Across the 13 Figure 2A markers with a registered DE row, seven plotted expression directions agree and six differ, with two sham libraries in the figure and three in the registered analysis.

manualReview.summary: The registered result reproduces the reported directions of Avp and Oxt. Agreement is mixed across the displayed hypothalamic markers.
manualReview.note: Figure 2A/B and the accompanying text report lower Avp and Oxt after lesion. Registered edgeR log2 fold changes are −0.7931 for Avp and −1.5848 for Oxt, with BH FDRs of 0.9064 and 0.7220. Seven of 13 paired heatmap marker directions agree. The per-library colours and FPKM bars support a directional check only. The original DESeq2 coefficient table, tested universe and per-gene P/FDR remain unavailable in the searched sources.
reviewFlags: The figure shows three PEL and two sham libraries. Figure 2B means and Figure 2A sample patterns identify the plotted controls as deposited SHAM-2 and SHAM-3. The registered result also includes SHAM-1. The authors' DESeq2 sample membership and animal-to-library assignments remain unconfirmed.

Six descriptive marker directions differ. The methods name DESeq2 and BH correction, and also refer to raw P < 0.05. The relationship between the reported HISAT2/featureCounts workflow and the CLC processing described in GEO is unclear.

The GEO download is hashed. The legacy local input retains its existing structural source match. Selected marker directions and incomplete author statistics limit author concordance and full verification.

verificationReview.reason: Direct comparison closes the review for selected directions. Both named downregulated genes have negative registered effects. Six of 13 paired heatmap directions differ, and none of the 13 meets registered FDR < 0.05. Plotted and registered cohorts differ. The available files do not identify the samples used for the fitted author coefficients or give the corresponding gene-level inference.
verificationReview.nextStep: For full reconciliation, which GSMs and biological replicates entered the hypothalamic PEL day-10 minus sham DESeq2 coefficient, specifically did it omit GSM7178967 as Figure 2 does? Request the fitted input and contrast definition, the discovery rule, and the full tested-gene export with gene IDs, log2 fold changes, raw P, adjusted P and missing tests.

comparabilityReview.basis: Compare the two explicit RNA-seq directions in the Results with registered edgeR logFC. Assess the broader Figure 2A panel separately by averaging the displayed per-library colour-scale positions within each arm and comparing directions. Use the original GEO FPKM only to corroborate the plotted samples and marker patterns.
comparabilityReview.reference: Wu et al., Translational Psychiatry (2024), DOI 10.1038/s41398-024-02930-y. Hypothalamic Results and Figure 2A/B on published page 5, with Supplementary Figure S2I and the accession-linked GSE229838 matrix and GSM records.

cohort.note: Both use mouse hypothalamus. Figure 2 shows three PEL and two sham libraries. Its control means and column patterns map to GSM7178968 and GSM7178969. Registered edgeR includes these and GSM7178967. S2I marks an unlabeled sham outlier. Public evidence establishes the plotted subset but leaves the fitted DESeq2 sample manifest and the number of independent animals per library unresolved.

contrast.note: Untreated PEL at day 10 minus sham-operated hypothalamus. GEO labels the retained PEL samples day 10 and sham samples day 0. GH treatment, the day-3 lesion and hippocampal assays are outside this comparison.

features.note: Both explicitly named genes map uniquely. Of 17 displayed marker labels, 15 resolve through deposited Ensembl IDs and the registered feature map. Mch and Gnrh correspond to Pmch and Gnrh1. Deposited Gh1 maps to Gh. Prl and Gh lack a displayed registered DE row. Glu and Gaba have no unique gene identifier in the figure.

effects.note: Both author-named downregulated genes have negative registered coefficients. Of 13 descriptive heatmap directions, seven agree and six differ. The six are Trh, Pmch, Pomc, Chat, Th and Ghrh. Adding the third sham flips the deposited mean-FPKM direction for five of those six, with Chat the exception. No original fitted author log2 fold changes are available for magnitude or correlation assessment.

inference.note: The authors report DESeq2 1.10.1 with BH adjustment. Figure 2A gives adjusted P < 0.05, while the methods also mention P < 0.05. Panel B's t-test concerns FPKM. The registered edgeR quasi-likelihood fit yields BH FDRs of 0.9064 (Avp) and 0.7220 (Oxt). Exact author raw P and FDR remain unassessed for every gene. A heatmap row alone does not establish a per-gene discovery.

coverage.note: Both explicit genes and 13 of 17 displayed marker labels were paired. The paper reports 499 up and seven down. Registered output has 287 BH discoveries in 14,575 displayed rows from a 14,590-feature BH family. All 287 registered discoveries lie outside the 13 paired rows. Author statistics and full-list overlap remain unknown.

comparabilityReview.criteria: Use every Figure 2A row, retain unresolved IDs and absent output rows, and fix orientation as lesion minus sham. Assess named DE directions and descriptive expression patterns separately. Author-concordance-v2 requires at least 30 paired genes and 90% relevant coverage plus a qualifying correlation or direction route and compatible cohort and effect definitions. No fitted author coefficient, per-gene P or adjusted P is imputed.
comparabilityReview.conclusion: The two explicit directions agree. The marker panel has mixed directional agreement across different sham cohorts. The public material supports this selected comparison, with no eligible effect-size spec or fully verified contrast.

computed.claim: Text-identified downregulated genes and registered statistics

computed.value: 17 displayed, 15 stable-ID mappings, 13 paired and seven directions agreeing. Six differ, two labels are ambiguous and two mapped genes have no registered DE row. Zero of the 13 meet registered FDR < 0.05.

computed.claim: Plotted controls identified from Figure 2B and Figure 2A independently of registered DE
computed.value: The Avp and Oxt sham means of SHAM-2 and SHAM-3 are 181.546 and 155.731 FPKM. The bars digitize to approximately 182 and 156. Both markers distinguish this pair from every alternative. The same ordered pair agrees in 104/104 non-tied within-marker sample orderings involving a sham, with one tie.

computed.claim: Effect of restoring the third sham on descriptive FPKM directions
computed.value: Five of the six discordant marker directions change sign when SHAM-1 is added to the plotted FPKM comparison. Chat retains its plotted direction.

computed.claim: Discovery counts and unassessed author coverage
computed.value: Manuscript 499 up, seven down. Registered 287 BH discoveries among 14,575 displayed DE rows, with 14,590 fit rows in the BH family. No complete author list or gene-wise FDR was available.

22,274 GEO feature rows, 59 columns, 24 FPKM columns and 24 estimated-count columns. All 24 GSM records have zero sample-table rows and no sample supplement. The series matrix has zero feature rows. ENA lists 24 runs and zero submitted analyses under the project query.

Publisher, PMC Open Data and the Europe PMC export contain the same DOCX, SHA-256 6bea41a21b88a748c86c1cc340ffd402a59ee94911430a42354257c6806a9c24. It contains four supplementary figure images and zero Word tables or embedded workbook files.

openIssues: The figure identifies the omitted plotted sham as GSM7178967 by inference. Whether that library also was excluded from the fitted DESeq2 comparison, and how libraries map to independent animals, require the authors' sample manifest.
The complete author DESeq2 export, tested-gene universe and exact discovery rule remain unavailable. Genome-wide effect agreement, per-gene author P/FDR and full discovery overlap remain unassessed.
